candidate_relations.reason: HHRH is caused by a primary renal phosphate-wasting defect leading to compensatory elevated 1,25(OH)2D, suppressed PTH, hypercalciuria, and nephrocalcinosis with undetectable/low FGF23. XLH is driven by elevated FGF23 which suppresses 1,25(OH)2D production, yielding low or inappropriately normal 1,25(OH)2D and no hypercalciuria or nephrocalcinosis. The candidate asserts XLH and misattributes the undetectable FGF23 finding, making it an incompatible subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: X-linked hypophosphatemia is a distinct subtype of hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with a different pathophysiology; the label also incorrectly characterizes FGF23 as undetectable, which conflicts with XLH (where FGF23 is elevated/normal), and the clinical profile here (elevated 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, low PTH, nephrocalcinosis, undetectable FGF23) is characteristic of HHRH (SLC34A3/NaPi-IIc mutations), not XLH

case_quality_flags: Undetectable FGF23 with elevated 1,25(OH)2D and nephrocalcinosis is pathognomonic for HHRH, clearly distinguishing it from XLH and other FGF23-mediated phosphaturic disorders.
